Figure 1:Progressive audiovisual generation sustained over an hour.Top: MiniMax-H3 denoises high-resolution clips and passes a frame to the next clip, while TaoMate uses few-step fixed-resolution generation with persistent audiovisual memory.TaoMate-HDrefines each chunk through two low-resolution evaluations and one high-resolution evaluation, passing each stage’s audiovisual prediction to the next chunk.
Retained history supports speech continuation as text windows advance.
L/H denote low/high video grids.
Bottom: full frames from two 60-minute,1376×7681376\times 768audiovisual streams at the labeled times (minutes:seconds).
The sampled frames preserve character appearance and scene composition across the hour.

Figure 2:A chunk’s refinement becomes the next chunk’s history.TheN=3N=3configuration shown here uses two coarse-grid evaluations followed by high-resolution refinement.
Each stage estimates a clean AV endpoint and encodes it on its native grid for the same stage of the next chunk, enabling the parallel execution shown at lower right.
Audio keeps its latent geometry throughout.
The lower-left panel shows training: selected-stage predictions form a high-resolution sequence for the two distillation scores.
The generator and scores share scene and speaker conditions, with role-specific dialogue windows.

Figure 3:Long-form audio-video generation, shown at 60 seconds.
The corresponding quantitative comparison appears in Table1.

Figure 4:Spatial detail across generation resolutions.Representative frames compare direct 480p, direct 768p, and progressive 480-to-768p generation on the same inputs.
Enlarged foreground regions reveal hand contours and product surfaces.
Progressive generation retains fine detail comparable to direct 768p generation while concentrating denoising on the coarse grid.

Figure 5:Text windows and generated speech.The input strip shows the overlapping windows supplied toTaoMate-HD, with the shared spanBBas the reference excerpt.
Thumbnail strips span each video, and colored intervals mark the transcribed excerpts.
Its transcripts show a repeated clause (left) and an incorrect sentence continuation (right).
Orange marks the affected phrases.
